chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The penalties that are for Allah cannot be excused except by the Imam. As for what is from the rights of the people regarding a penalty, there is no problem if one is excused from it, except by the Imam.
ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to excuse from divine penalties (hudud) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisdiction of the Imam in waiving hudud, distinguishing between rights of Allah (haqq Allah) which require the Imam's authority for pardon, and rights of people (haqq al-nas) which others may forgive. This distinction underpins the Shia legal theory regarding the Imam's exclusive role in dispensing divine penalties, reflecting the theological view that the Imam acts as the vicegerent of Allah in enforcing divine law. The ruling highlights the balance between divine sovereignty and human agency in the context of judicial mercy.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zureys Al Kunasy, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘None can excuse from the Penalties which are for the Sake of Allahazwj, besides the Imamasws. So as for what was from the rights of the people regarding a Penalty (Hadd), so there is no problem if one excuses from it, besides the Imamasws’.
